#Media elements

How <video> and <audio> work in Wren, beyond the generated API reference (api/htmlmedia.md, api/media.md, api/mse.md). Everything here is native: the state machine, the track model, the WebVTT parser, the subtitle layer and the frame callbacks are Odin in src/page and src/media; no JavaScript of the browser implements them.

#The player

A media element (src/page/media_element.odin) runs the HTML resource-selection and load algorithms over a media.Player (src/media), which decodes on its own threads. Codecs: H.264 and HEVC and AAC through Media Foundation (DXVA on the GPU when the system has it), AV1 and VP9 in software when the system has no decoder (see portability.md), Opus, Vorbis, FLAC, MP3, PCM. Containers: MP4 and WebM, progressive (a download) or through Media Source Extensions.

#Audio, video and text tracks

element.audioTracks, videoTracks and textTracks (src/page/media_tracks.odin, media_texttracks.odin) expose the tracks the container announced and the text tracks of <track> and addTextTrack. The lists are EventTargets (addtrack, removetrack, change); AudioTrack / VideoTrack carry id, kind, label, language and the enabled / selected flags. The chosen tracks start enabled. Changing which audio or video track is active is recorded and passed to the player (media.player_select_audio / player_select_video); the progressive and MSE players decode a single stream, so a mid-stream switch to another track of the same resource takes effect only where a future multi-stream player can honour it — the state a script reads is always correct.

Turned off by media.tracks.enabled (the lists are then empty and tracks stay implicit).

#Text tracks, WebVTT and subtitles

A <track kind srclang label default src> loads its src as WebVTT, parsed natively (src/media/webvtt.odin): the signature line, NOTE comments, REGION and STYLE blocks, and the cues — their identifier, the timing line with its settings (vertical, line, position, size, align) and the payload with its inline markup (<b> <i> <u> <c.class> <v Name> <lang> <ruby>/<rt> and internal timestamps). TextTrack.mode is disabled / hidden / showing; addTextTrack, addCue, removeCue, VTTCue and TextTrackCueList are all supported. The <track> element fires load / error and exposes readyState.

Which cues are active is tracked by the player's clock (no script polling): cuechange fires on a track and enter / exit on a cue when the active set changes. The cues of showing tracks are drawn over the video by the shell (src/browser/video_shell.odin), in a layer of the page over the picture: the ::cue defaults (white text on a translucent black box, near the bottom), honouring the cue's align. Turned off by media.subtitles.enabled; media.subtitles.max_lines caps how many cue lines are drawn at once.

#requestVideoFrameCallback

video.requestVideoFrameCallback(callback) (src/page/media_rvfc.odin) runs callback(now, metadata) once, the next time a new decoded picture is presented on screen — the same moment the getVideoPlaybackQuality counters advance, the real presentation path, not a timer. The VideoFrameCallbackMetadata gives presentationTime, expectedDisplayTime, width, height, mediaTime, presentedFrames and processingDuration (0, not measured); captureTime, receiveTime and rtpTimestamp are never present (Wren is not a WebRTC endpoint). cancelVideoFrameCallback(id) cancels. media.video_frame_callbacks.max caps how many may wait on one video.

#Managed Media Source

ManagedMediaSource, ManagedSourceBuffer and BufferedChangeEvent (src/page/media_managed.odin) are the managed variant of MSE, where the user agent says when to stream. ManagedMediaSource.streaming is true while Wren wants data; it fires startstreaming once less than media.mse.managed.low_seconds is buffered ahead of the playback position and endstreaming once media.mse.managed.high_seconds is. A ManagedSourceBuffer fires bufferedchange with the ranges added and removed whenever its buffered ranges change (an append or an eviction). Everything of plain MSE applies (api/mse.md).

#The video fast path

A <video> is painted inside the page's paint pass, so a long script that holds the interface thread freezes the video with the rest of the page (YouTube runs a ~85 ms task every few seconds). browser.video.fast_path keeps the video moving: during a chrome frame (the browser's interface drawn while a page is busy, see chrome-style.md and src/browser/shell_frames.odin), the video's newest decoded picture is drawn over the page's last frame at the video's box, recomposing only the video — no script runs and the page is not laid out again. It runs only for a video that fills its box opaquely with nothing drawn over it, so the overlay can never show a pixel the normal path would not have; otherwise the picture is left frozen (a freeze beats a wrong frame).

Values: auto (on), off (the video freezes with the page), verify (a diagnostic that reports in the console when the fast path is recomposing, for comparing against off). Implemented in src/browser/video_fast_path.odin.
